hero.headline: India's Skyroot Aerospace launches Vikram-1 rocket in space ambitions push
hero.body:
India's first space-tech unicorn Skyroot Aerospace successfully launched its Vikram-1 rocket on Saturday, marking a significant milestone in the country's growing commercial space sector. The launch represents a step forward in India's ambitions to transform its position in the global space industry through private sector participation.

Skyroot Aerospace achieved unicorn status as a privately held startup valued at over one billion dollars, becoming the first Indian space technology company to reach that threshold. The Vikram-1 launch demonstrates the company's technical capabilities in rocket development and orbital delivery systems.

The successful flight comes as India expands its space program beyond government-led initiatives. Private companies like Skyroot are developing commercial launch capabilities that could provide lower-cost access to orbit for satellites and other payloads. The launch vehicle is designed to carry small satellites into various orbital configurations.

India has been building its space technology sector following regulatory reforms that opened the industry to private investment and operations. The government has encouraged commercial space ventures while maintaining its own robust program through the Indian Space Research Organisation, which has conducted missions to the Moon and Mars.

The Vikram-1 launch positions Skyroot among a growing number of private space companies worldwide developing small to medium-lift rockets for the commercial satellite market. The success of this mission could attract additional investment to India's space sector and demonstrate the country's capabilities in manufacturing and operating orbital launch systems.

cards.headline: U.S. Strikes Iran for Seventh Straight Night as Shipping Halts in Strait of Hormuz
cards.body:
The U.S. military completed its seventh consecutive night of strikes against Iranian targets on Friday, with operations designed to "continue degrading Iranian military capabilities," according to U.S. Central Command. The escalating campaign has expanded well beyond military installations to include critical civilian infrastructure, raising serious humanitarian concerns.

American warplanes struck bridges in Iran's southern Hormozgan province, killing at least seven people according to Iranian state television. The bridges served as a key transit point for Bandar Abbas, Iran's main port. Additional strikes targeted a tower at Chabahar port on the Gulf of Oman, which the U.S. military claimed the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps used to coordinate attacks on vessels. Electrical infrastructure and Iranshahr airport also came under fire.

By Friday morning, Iranian health officials reported at least 38 deaths and more than 400 wounded from the American strikes. Iran's energy ministry urged citizens to reduce electricity and air conditioning usage after U.S. attacks strained the power grid, with southern regions experiencing "extreme heat and attacks on power infrastructure."

Iran has responded with its own strikes across the region. The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps targeted a U.S. air base in Bahrain, an intelligence facility, a naval fuel pier in Kuwait, and communications centers in Kuwait and Qatar. Kuwait suspended operations at its international airport following Iranian missile and drone attacks and confirmed that a power and desalination plant was hit, damaging the facility that provides about 90 percent of the country's drinking water.

The targeting of civilian infrastructure has drawn scrutiny from human rights experts, with some warning that strikes on nonmilitary facilities could constitute war crimes. The IRGC issued a statement warning of a "very severe and devastating price to pay" for countries hosting U.S. bases if attacks on civilians and civilian infrastructure continued.

Shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, which handles roughly a fifth of global oil and gas supply, has drastically reduced in recent days as violence escalated. Though a memorandum of understanding signed last month stated the strait should remain open to traffic, both nations interpreted the agreement differently, with competing plans for vessel transit.

The renewed fighting represents the unraveling of a ceasefire between the two nations. President Trump reportedly met with senior officials this week to discuss an expanded aerial campaign aimed at forcing Iran to reopen the strait. The conflict has now entered its seventh day, with both sides showing no signs of de-escalation. Iran has asked allied Houthi forces in Yemen to prepare to close the oil route through the Red Sea if the U.S. continues targeting Iranian energy infrastructure, a potential action that analysts warn could paralyze global energy markets.

cards.headline: Iranian strikes injure US troops at Jordan bases
cards.teaser: Several American service members were injured when Iranian forces attacked at least two military installations in Jordan this week.
cards.body:
Iranian attacks struck at least two US military facilities in Jordan this week, injuring several American service members, according to CBS News.

The US and Jordan reported no deaths from the incidents. Iran has continued retaliatory strikes across the region, including attacks on infrastructure in Kuwait. The escalating exchanges between the US and Iran have expanded to include strikes on bridges and renewed tensions over control of the Strait of Hormuz.

cards.headline: Over 100 House Democrats vote to block military aid to Israel
cards.teaser: A significant portion of House Democrats voted against billions of dollars in military assistance to Israel, exposing divisions within the party.
cards.body:
More than 100 Democrats in the House of Representatives voted to block billions of dollars in military aid to Israel. The vote reflected a growing divide within the Democratic Party over US policy toward Israel and military assistance.

AIPAC closed its donor portal to Democrats who voted to end aid to Israel following the vote. Representative Smith said he faced pressure from violent, far-left activists to vote against the aid package. The vote highlighted sharp divisions in Congress over the issue of US support for Israel.

cards.headline: Trump releases classified documents on election security, claims vulnerabilities exist
cards.teaser: President Trump declassified intelligence documents alleging foreign election interference capabilities, though agencies found no votes were altered in 2020.
cards.body:
President Trump delivered a speech releasing selectively declassified documents about election security, alleging that China interfered in the 2020 election he lost to Joe Biden. He highlighted potential vulnerabilities in American voting systems. China denied the allegations, calling them fabricated.

The intelligence community has maintained that no votes were altered in the 2020 election. Democratic officials criticized the disclosure as an attempt to undermine confidence in upcoming elections. The documents presented largely did not reveal new information or provide evidence that past election results were fraudulent or that actual interference changed previous outcomes.

cards.headline: Zelenskyy Weighs Replacing Top Military Commander as Protests Continue
cards.teaser: Ukraine's president is considering dismissing his commander-in-chief as public demonstrations over recent military leadership changes enter their second day.
cards.body:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has defended his recent dismissal of Defence Minister Mykhailo Fedorov, a reformist figure popular among military ranks. At a press conference with British Prime Minister Keir Starmer, Zelenskyy acknowledged a breakdown in relations between Fedorov and Col Gen Oleksandr Syrskyi, the country's commander-in-chief, describing their dialogue as "challenging." Zelenskyy stated he had to choose between the two sides.

The dismissal has triggered significant protests from Ukrainian soldiers and the public, who oppose the removal of the defence minister. Reports indicate Zelenskyy is now considering whether to replace Syrskyi as well, as the leadership tensions continue amid Ukraine's ongoing war with Russia.

cards.headline: Trump proposes tariffs on Canada over wildfire smoke crossing into US
cards.body:
Former President Donald Trump announced plans to impose tariffs on Canada in response to wildfire smoke drifting across the border into American cities. In a post on Truth Social, Trump said the cost of the pollution "must of necessity be added to the TARIFFS Canada is currently paying."

The proposal marks an expansion of tariff policy into environmental concerns, using trade measures to address cross-border air quality issues. Canadian wildfires have sent massive smoke plumes across the United States in recent years, affecting air quality in cities from the Midwest to the East Coast. About 109 million people faced poor air quality across the midwest, mid-Atlantic and northeast as smoke blanketed major cities. In Detroit and Chicago, residents were warned to stay indoors after air quality indexes reached hazardous levels of 361. Washington DC, Baltimore, New York City and Philadelphia also experienced very unhealthy to hazardous air quality readings.

Trump characterized the smoke as "dirty air" and said he planned to call Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney to discuss Ottawa's plans for managing the blazes. Republican Senator Bernie Moreno of Ohio announced plans to introduce legislation to sanction Canada and Canadian government officials, claiming Canada had "failed to invest in wildfire prevention methods including forest thinning, fuel reduction, prescribed burns, and stronger enforcement against arson."

Four Republican House members representing Michigan also wrote to Carney, stating that if Canada would not manage its forests to prevent fires, "the United States will look elsewhere, and act on our own, to protect our people."

Carney responded to the accusations by stating that "fighting climate change is the responsibility of all countries, including the United States." Ontario Premier Doug Ford suggested the US offer more aid instead of complaining, noting that Canada had previously provided support to the US during similar situations. "Maybe what you should do rather than complain is send support, send help," Ford said.

Large fires are also burning across the US in what authorities deem an above-average fire year. More than 5,740 square miles of US land has burned from wildfires so far this year, 31 percent more than the average of the previous decade. Wildfires in Minnesota, Oregon, Washington and Idaho have contributed to smoke affecting both countries as prevailing wind patterns carry smoke across borders.

Scientists link increased wildfire activity to climate change driven by human activities, which is causing warmer, drier conditions and lengthening fire seasons. The US is the world's largest oil and gas producer and has historically emitted more greenhouse gases than any other country. The Trump administration has recently rolled back environmental protections while bolstering the fossil fuel industry and targeting renewable energy programs.

cards.headline: Ukrainian Drone Strike Kills Seven Workers at Russian Warehouse
cards.teaser: Ukrainian drones struck a warehouse operated by Russia's largest online retailer and ignited a fire at an oil depot near Moscow.
cards.body:
Ukrainian forces conducted a large-scale drone operation targeting Moscow and surrounding regions, with the city's mayor reporting around 200 drones involved in the assault. Seven warehouse workers were killed when drones struck a Wildberries facility, Russia's largest online retailer, in the Moscow region. Ukraine's leadership characterized the Wildberries warehouses near Moscow and in Tambov as major logistics facilities supplying sanctioned components.

The attacks also ignited a fire at an oil depot in the Moscow region. These strikes represent part of Ukraine's ongoing aerial campaign against energy infrastructure and military targets inside Russia, designed to undermine Moscow's war effort.

cards.headline: Zelenskyy Weighs Replacing Top Military Commander as Protests Continue
cards.teaser: Ukraine's president is considering dismissing his commander-in-chief as public demonstrations over recent military leadership changes enter their second day.
cards.body:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has defended his recent dismissal of Defence Minister Mykhailo Fedorov, a reformist figure popular among military ranks. At a press conference with British Prime Minister Keir Starmer, Zelenskyy acknowledged a breakdown in relations between Fedorov and Col Gen Oleksandr Syrskyi, the country's commander-in-chief, describing their dialogue as "challenging." Zelenskyy stated he had to choose between the two sides.

The dismissal has triggered significant protests from Ukrainian soldiers and the public, who oppose the removal of the defence minister. Reports indicate Zelenskyy is now considering whether to replace Syrskyi as well, as the leadership tensions continue amid Ukraine's ongoing war with Russia.

cards.headline: Israel Launches Campaign to Counter Iranian Online Recruitment
cards.teaser: Israeli authorities have implemented countermeasures against what they describe as Iranian efforts to recruit agents through online platforms.
cards.body:
The Israeli government has enacted a broad set of countermeasures aimed at containing Iranian online recruitment operations, according to Israeli authorities. Officials describe the Iranian efforts as systematic attempts by Iranian agents to recruit Israelis through internet platforms. The Israeli response includes public warnings about the recruitment campaigns.

The countermeasures represent an acknowledgment by Israeli security services that Iran has developed sophisticated online intelligence operations targeting Israeli citizens. Israeli authorities characterized the Iranian recruitment efforts as a significant espionage threat requiring a coordinated national response beyond traditional counterintelligence methods.

cards.headline: Indian Police Forcibly Remove Activist from Hunger Strike
cards.teaser: Authorities removed Sonam Wangchuk from a hunger strike he began last month to protest educational mismanagement affecting millions of students.
cards.body:
Indian police forcibly removed activist Sonam Wangchuk to a hospital after he had been on a hunger strike for 20 days. Wangchuk launched the strike last month to protest educational mismanagement affecting millions of students across India.

Following Wangchuk's removal, Abhijeet Dipke, founder of the Cockroach Janta Party, began an indefinite fast in his place to continue the campaign for educational reform.

cards.headline: Laos Unable to Determine Cause of Tourist Deaths Linked to Methanol
cards.teaser: Officials say they have no evidence of poisoning in deaths of foreign tourists because autopsies were not conducted.
cards.body:
Laotian officials say they cannot establish the cause of death for foreign tourists who died in 2024 in cases linked to methanol poisoning, citing the absence of autopsies. Without these medical examinations, authorities state they lack evidence to prove poisoning occurred.

Several countries, including Denmark, have reported that Laos filed minor charges related to the deaths. Parents of two Australian teenagers killed after consuming tainted liquor at a hostel have criticized the charges as inadequate. Australia subsequently updated its travel guidance for Laos following the announcement of charges.

cards.headline: Freedom Convoy Leader Seeks Permission for International Travel
cards.teaser: Tamara Lich, currently under house arrest, has requested permission to travel internationally including to the White House and on a cruise.
cards.body:
Tamara Lich, a leader of the Freedom Convoy who is under house arrest, has requested permission for international travel that would include a visit to the White House. Prosecutors say Lich is seeking what amounts to a blank check for international travel, including a cruise. The request comes as she serves a sentence related to her role in organizing the protest.

Prosecutors argue that Lich is attempting to profit from the very protest that led to her criminal sentence. The Freedom Convoy leader's travel request would represent a significant loosening of the restrictions imposed as part of her house arrest conditions. Canadian authorities are evaluating whether to grant the international travel permissions.

cards.teaser: A significant portion of House Democrats voted against billions of dollars in military assistance to Israel, exposing divisions within the party.

More than 100 Democrats in the House of Representatives voted to block billions of dollars in military aid to Israel. The vote reflected a growing divide within the Democratic Party over US policy toward Israel and military assistance.

AIPAC closed its donor portal to Democrats who voted to end aid to Israel following the vote. Representative Smith said he faced pressure from violent, far-left activists to vote against the aid package. The vote highlighted sharp divisions in Congress over the issue of US support for Israel.

cards.headline: Digital cameras from 2000s gain popularity among younger users
cards.teaser: People who were not alive 25 years ago are purchasing digital cameras from the early 2000s era.
cards.body:
Digital cameras from the 2000s are experiencing a resurgence in popularity, particularly among younger consumers who didn't grow up with the devices. The revival is driven by several factors: cyclical fashion trends, childhood nostalgia, fatigue with smartphone photography, and celebrity influence—notably Taylor Swift, who has been associated with the retro camera trend.

These older devices offer a distinct aesthetic and shooting experience that differs from modern smartphone cameras, attracting users seeking an alternative approach to digital photography.

cards.headline: Ukrainian drones kill eight in strikes on Russian regions
cards.teaser: Kyiv targeted energy infrastructure and military sites inside Russia, killing eight people and wounding more than 60.
cards.body:
Ukrainian drone strikes on Russian regions killed eight people and wounded more than 60 others. The attacks targeted energy infrastructure and military sites as part of Kyiv's ongoing aerial campaign against Russia.

The strikes hit Wildberries retail warehouses located near Moscow and in Tambov. Ukraine's leader characterized these facilities as major logistics centers that supply sanctioned components supporting Russia's war effort. The drone campaign is designed to disrupt Moscow's military operations by attacking infrastructure critical to its logistics network.

cards.headline: Woman describes life inside Jeffrey Epstein operation
cards.teaser: A former assistant gave a rare account of how the convicted sex offender lured and abused those who worked for him.
cards.body:
A woman identified as "Anya" has given the BBC a rare firsthand account of working for convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein. She described experiencing control, threats, and being pressured into disfiguring surgery while employed by the financier.

Anya's interview provides an insider perspective on Epstein's methods of manipulation and abuse targeting those in his employ. Her testimony documents the experiences of people who worked closely with him during his years of criminal activity.

cards.headline: Laos says cause of tourist deaths cannot be determined
cards.teaser: Officials said they have no evidence of poisoning in 2024 deaths linked to methanol because autopsies were not performed.
cards.body:
Original Card (Unchanged)

Laos officials announced they cannot determine the cause of tourist deaths in 2024 that were linked to methanol. Authorities said they lack evidence of poisoning because autopsies were not conducted on the deceased visitors.

The deaths raised concerns about safety for tourists in Laos and the availability of contaminated alcohol. Without autopsy results, officials have been unable to confirm methanol poisoning as the cause of death despite initial suspicions linking the cases to tainted beverages.

---

Note: The Guardian source provided is about sun exposure and health benefits—a completely different topic from the Laos tourist deaths story. Therefore, the original card text is returned unchanged per your instructions.

cards.headline: British Energy Secretary to announce new North Sea drilling plans
cards.teaser: Andy Burnham will outline proposals for oil and gas drilling after the Labour manifesto pledged not to issue new licenses.
cards.body:
Energy Secretary Andy Burnham is set to announce new proposals for oil and gas drilling in the North Sea. This move creates tension within the Labour Party, which pledged in its 2024 manifesto not to issue new drilling licenses.

The announcement highlights the government's challenge in balancing energy security with its climate commitments and previous campaign promises.

hero.headline: SpaceX Stock Falls After Analysts Release Price Targets Following Starship Launch Abort
hero.teaser: Shares of SpaceX dropped back to initial public offering levels shortly after Wall Street analysts published price targets for the space company.
hero.body:
SpaceX shares have declined below their initial public offering price of $135 per share, closing at $131.11 during Thursday trading. The drop marks a significant retreat from the company's peak market value of over $2.6 trillion in the first three days after its mid-June listing, which was the largest debut in stock market history.

The share price decline has affected major investors worldwide. Australian billionaire Gina Rinehart's company, Hancock Prospecting, purchased over $1 billion worth of SpaceX shares at the IPO. Based on the stock's peak value, Rinehart has experienced a paper loss of approximately $500 million, with an additional $30 million in losses following Thursday's close.

Elon Musk's personal net worth has fallen to $838 billion as of Thursday, according to Forbes. This represents a significant decline from when Musk briefly became the world's first trillionaire following the IPO announcement.

Short sellers have benefited substantially from the stock's decline. Bloomberg reported that investors betting against SpaceX have recorded profits of $3.88 billion as shares have fallen in seven of the last eight trading sessions. The company experienced its largest single-day drop on June 22 when it announced plans to issue billions in additional debt through bonds.

Despite the losses, major investors appear to be holding their positions for the long term. Hancock Prospecting has not indicated whether it has sold any of its stake. A spokesperson for the company declined to comment on whether it has bought or sold additional shares since the listing, though it has republished articles about its initial investment on its website.

Market analysts suggest that long-term investors view the decline as a temporary pullback in what they consider a growth opportunity. Tony Sycamore, a market analyst at IG Australia, noted that investors backing SpaceX were typically looking at a decade-long investment horizon rather than short-term gains.

The IPO generated unprecedented retail interest in Australia. CommSec, the country's largest retail share broker, received applications from 28,000 Australians seeking to purchase SpaceX shares, setting a record for applications. The company received three times more applications globally than it could accommodate. While CommSec declined to disclose exactly how many Australian applicants successfully purchased shares, the level of interest exceeded previous IPO records by a significant margin.

Market analysts attributed the recent stock decline to easing investor euphoria rather than fundamental company concerns. Some retail investors who participated in early trading likely sold at the peak to lock in profits, while others appear committed to holding their shares through the company's long-term development.

cards.headline: Stock Markets Fall as Semiconductor Selloff Spreads Across Tech Sector
cards.teaser: Major US stock indexes closed lower on Friday, with the Nasdaq and S&P 500 each dropping more than 1 percent as a selloff in semiconductor stocks spread anxiety.
cards.body:
Major US stock indexes closed lower on Friday, with the Nasdaq and S&P 500 each dropping more than 1 percent. The decline extended losses from earlier in the week as a semiconductor selloff rippled through the technology sector, driven by concerns about artificial intelligence spending and competitive pressures in the chip industry.

The downturn followed news of technological advances from China in artificial intelligence, which unsettled investor confidence in US tech stocks. Semiconductor companies, which have benefited significantly from AI-related investment over the past year, led the selloff. Analysts cautioned that questions about the sustainability of heavy AI infrastructure spending could intensify the rout as investors reassess whether current valuations reflect realistic growth prospects.

cards.headline: Russia Sanctions Bill Raises Concerns Over Dollar's Global Role
cards.teaser: Legislation broadening sanctions against Russia has sparked debate about whether aggressive economic measures could undermine the US dollar's international dominance.
cards.body:
The Trump administration has broadened sanctions legislation against Russia while simultaneously scaling back some measures as adversaries develop workarounds to American economic pressure.

Experts worry that aggressive use of sanctions as a foreign policy tool may accelerate other nations' efforts to reduce their reliance on dollar-based transactions. As countries seek alternatives to conduct international trade outside the dollar system, analysts believe this trend could erode the U.S. dollar's dominance in global finance.

cards.headline: Taylor Farms Pulls Lettuce Products After Parasite Outbreak Linked to Supply
cards.teaser: The California produce company is removing lettuce from the market after its products were connected to cases of cyclosporiasis.
cards.body:
Taylor Farms voluntarily removed all iceberg lettuce sourced from central Mexico from the US market following a cyclosporiasis outbreak. The parasitic infection sickened approximately 1,645 people across five states who consumed Taco Bell products containing the contaminated lettuce. Major buyers including Taco Bell and food distributor Sysco pulled Taylor Farms lettuce from their supply chains in response.

The FDA is investigating how the lettuce became contaminated and plans to inspect farms and a lettuce shredding facility to trace the source of the parasite and determine where the affected products were distributed.

cards.headline: Robinhood CEO Discusses Trump Accounts and Defends Trading Platform
cards.teaser: Vlad Tenev is working to attract the next generation of American investors through new account features bearing the former president's name.
cards.body:
Vlad Tenev, chief executive of Robinhood, is promoting the platform's new Trump-branded accounts to appeal to younger investors. The digital brokerage aims to expand its reach within the next generation of Americans entering the stock market.

Tenev has defended Robinhood against criticism comparing day trading to gambling. He argues the platform provides retail investors with legitimate access to financial markets, positioning it as a serious investment tool rather than a speculative betting service.

cards.headline: World Cup Final Drives Record Betting on Prediction Markets
cards.teaser: The soccer tournament has propelled Kalshi and Polymarket to new user records in what may become the largest gambling event in history.
cards.body:
The World Cup final has generated billions of dollars in bets on prediction markets Kalshi and Polymarket, driving both platforms to new user records. The soccer tournament has created what industry observers believe may be the largest gambling event in history, as bettors worldwide place wagers on the outcome.

The surge in betting activity reflects the growing popularity of prediction markets as alternatives to traditional sportsbooks. Both Kalshi and Polymarket have seen significant growth in users and betting volume tied to the tournament, with the final match drawing unprecedented levels of wagering activity across their platforms.

cards.headline: Homebuyers Face Growing Problem of Last-Minute Price Reductions
cards.teaser: Gazundering, the practice of lowering an offer just before closing, is becoming more common in the property market.
cards.body:
Homebuyers are increasingly encountering gazundering, a practice where buyers reduce their offer at the last moment before contracts are exchanged. One seller reported that buyers dropped their offer by 15,000 pounds the day before exchange, illustrating the financial pressure this tactic creates for sellers who have already committed to their own onward purchases.

While still a small phenomenon, gazundering is growing as a problem in the property market. The practice takes advantage of sellers' vulnerable position late in the transaction process, when they have often already made commitments based on the agreed sale price. Industry experts are recommending steps sellers can take to protect themselves from last-minute price reductions.

cards.headline: Apple raises iCloud+ subscription prices in multiple countries
cards.teaser: Apple increased prices for iCloud+ storage plans across eight countries, marking the service's first price adjustment in several markets.
cards.body:
Apple raised subscription prices for its iCloud+ cloud storage service in eight countries. The price increases affect various storage tiers of the iCloud+ service, which provides users with cloud backup and storage capabilities for photos, documents, and device data.

The pricing changes also extend to Apple Music streaming service and the bundled Apple One subscription package. Apple Music prices increased for the first time since 2022. The adjustments vary by country and storage tier, with the specific markets affected including several regions outside the United States.

cards.headline: Index Ventures co-founder predicts AI wealth redistribution
cards.teaser: Venture capitalist Neil Rimer says the wealth generated by artificial intelligence in Silicon Valley will need to be redistributed.
cards.body:
Neil Rimer, who co-founded venture capital firm Index Ventures, stated that the significant wealth being created by artificial intelligence companies in Silicon Valley will eventually be redistributed. Rimer predicted the redistribution could occur through voluntary or involuntary means.

The comments come as AI companies have driven substantial valuations and investor returns in the technology sector. Rimer's remarks address growing questions about wealth concentration in the AI industry and how economic gains from the technology will be distributed across society.

cards.headline: Vertu releases $6,880 Alphafold smartphone with AI agent for executives
cards.teaser: Luxury phone maker Vertu introduced the Alphafold foldable smartphone featuring an integrated AI agent designed for executive workflows.
cards.body:
Vertu launched the Alphafold, a luxury foldable smartphone priced at $6,880, designed for executives seeking AI-powered productivity tools. The device integrates an AI agent called Hermes that automates workflows and handles task management for business users.

Reviewers tested the Alphafold across key performance areas including its AI workflow capabilities, battery life, and security features. The phone represents Vertu's strategy to merge premium hardware with enterprise-focused artificial intelligence software at a premium price point.

cards.headline: Maricopa County reduces heat deaths despite extreme temperatures
cards.teaser: Arizona's Maricopa County has decreased heat-related deaths even as the desert region experiences some of the hottest temperatures.
cards.body:
Maricopa County in Arizona is tackling one of the most pressing public health challenges of the climate era. Despite experiencing some of the hottest temperatures in the region, the county has managed to reduce heat-related deaths through deliberate interventions and targeted strategies.

The county's success in lowering heat fatalities offers valuable lessons for other communities worldwide grappling with rising temperatures and intensifying heat waves. Maricopa County demonstrates that even in areas facing extreme baseline temperatures, coordinated efforts can effectively protect vulnerable populations and save lives.

cards.headline: Second half of summer forecast shows rain chances but continued heatwave risk
cards.teaser: Weather forecasts for late July and August suggest more changeable conditions while the threat of heatwaves persists.
cards.body:
Weather forecasts predict more changeable conditions during late July and August, with increased chances of rainfall across some areas. Despite this shift toward more unsettled weather patterns, meteorologists warn that the threat of heatwaves will persist throughout the remainder of summer.

The outlook suggests a transition from the more stable weather seen earlier in the season. Residents should prepare for a mix of conditions, with periods of extreme heat still likely alongside wetter spells in the coming weeks.

cards.headline: Canadian wildfires blanket US and Canadian cities with smoke
cards.teaser: Wildfires burning in Ontario have spread smoke across cities in both the United States and Canada, creating air quality concerns.
cards.body:
Smoke from Ontario wildfires is spreading across a vast region, affecting approximately 109 million people across the US midwest, mid-Atlantic and north-east. The smoke has blanketed major cities including Chicago and Detroit, where air quality indexes have reached hazardous levels. Authorities have warned residents to stay indoors and reduce activity levels due to the dangerous air conditions.

Air quality alerts have been issued across more than 20 US states as the smoke continues to drift southward. The widespread pollution is creating health risks for millions of Americans as smoke particles travel hundreds of miles from the burning areas in south-central Canada.

hero.headline: Caitlin Clark sets WNBA record with 45 points and 10 assists
hero.body:
Indiana Fever guard Caitlin Clark made WNBA history by becoming the first player to record at least 45 points and 10 assists in a single game. Clark finished with exactly 45 points and 10 assists as the Fever defeated the Seattle Storm 110-107 on Friday night, setting a new benchmark for individual performance in the league.

The 45-point output marked a career high for Clark and also set a new franchise record for the Fever. Her performance demonstrated her ability to excel across multiple statistical categories simultaneously. The game also saw Clark contribute four steals and two blocks, showcasing her defensive impact alongside her offensive dominance.

Clark's playmaking efficiency proved particularly remarkable. Distributing 10 assists while scoring 45 points requires exceptional court vision and the ability to create opportunities for teammates while maintaining offensive aggression. This combination had never been achieved before in WNBA history at such elite levels in a single contest.

The historic performance came during a period of heightened scrutiny surrounding Clark's professional career. Recent weeks have seen debates about officiating and physical play in the league, particularly following an incident involving Phoenix Mercury forward Alyssa Thomas, who hit Clark in the throat during a game. Thomas was later suspended for one game, though no foul was called at the time. The incident sparked broader conversations about player safety and fair officiating.

NBA Commissioner Adam Silver commented on the situation, saying that Clark has become a "political football" amid debates about officiating and physical play in the WNBA. Silver noted that the issues aren't largely about officiating itself, but rather broader concerns about how the league addresses these matters.

Beyond the record-setting performance, Clark also reached another milestone. She became the fastest player in WNBA history to make 200 career three-pointers, achieving this mark in just 74 games. This broke the previous record of 81 games set by Katie Smith.

Clark's transition from college basketball to the professional ranks has been closely watched by fans and media. Her college career at Iowa generated significant attention, and expectations followed her to Indiana. The historic performance provides concrete evidence of her impact at the professional level and her capacity to produce at volumes rarely seen in the league.

The Fever's victory over Seattle also carried playoff implications as teams position themselves for the postseason. Clark's ability to deliver in meaningful games adds another dimension to her value beyond the statistical milestone. The performance establishes a new standard for what constitutes an elite all-around offensive game in women's professional basketball.

cards.headline: New Zealand defeats Ireland to extend 32-year Eden Park winning streak
cards.teaser: The All Blacks scored five tries in a dominant performance to maintain their unbeaten home record.
cards.body:
New Zealand defeated Ireland 40-21 in a Nations Championship clash at Eden Park, extending their unbeaten streak at the venue to 53 matches across 32 years. The All Blacks dominated the first half, scoring four tries to establish a commanding 28-7 lead by halftime and ultimately securing their third consecutive victory in the inaugural Nations Championship.

Ireland's performance was hampered by an error-strewn opening, with missed tackles and handling mistakes proving costly against the ruthless hosts. The defeat marks the end of Ireland's season without breaking New Zealand's fortress record in Auckland.

cards.headline: Aston Villa signs Johan Manzambi in club-record deal
cards.teaser: The midfielder joined Villa for more than 50 million pounds as the club enters a new era.
cards.body:
Johan Manzambi has joined Aston Villa in a club-record transfer worth more than £50 million. The midfielder represents a significant financial investment as Villa enters a new chapter under their current project.

Manzambi is positioned as a key figure in the club's ambitions moving forward, with the transfer fee reflecting Villa's determination to strengthen their squad in the competitive transfer market.

cards.headline: Lionel Messi reacts to photo of himself with infant Lamine Yamal before World Cup final
cards.teaser: The Argentina star called it crazy that he will face Spain's Yamal after being photographed with him as a baby.
cards.body:
Updated Card:

Lionel Messi reflected on a striking coincidence ahead of Sunday's World Cup final against Spain: a photograph of him holding infant Lamine Yamal years before the young player became a professional footballer. The image has taken on prophetic significance as the two now face each other on sport's biggest stage.

Spain coach Luis de la Fuente commented on the moment's seeming destiny, suggesting such occurrences reveal something spiritual or purposeful beyond mere chance. Argentina head coach Lionel Scaloni praised the 39-year-old Messi as "pure history" ahead of the championship match.

cards.headline: Thomas Tuchel says England carries World Cup semifinal scars into playoff
cards.teaser: The England coach defended his tactics after the team's loss to Argentina in the World Cup semifinal.
cards.body:
England coach Thomas Tuchel said the team carries the psychological impact of its World Cup semifinal defeat as it prepares for a playoff match against France. Tuchel defended the tactical approach he employed in the loss to Argentina.

The German coach has faced scrutiny over his strategy in the semifinal. Tuchel stated that negative fan opinion will not change his conviction about how to manage the national team going forward.

cards.headline: Wayne Rooney rows down Hudson River with BBC pundits
cards.teaser: The former England captain took to the water with Joe Hart and Micah Richards in New York.
cards.body:
Wayne Rooney rowed down the Hudson River alongside fellow BBC pundits Joe Hart and Micah Richards. The three former professional footballers participated in the activity while in New York for World Cup coverage.

The Hudson River excursion came during the trio's broadcasting duties for the BBC. Rooney, Hart, and Richards have been working together as analysts during the tournament.

hero.headline: Christopher Nolan's 'The Odyssey' Draws Debate Over Hero Narrative and Historical Accuracy
hero.body:
Christopher Nolan has adapted Homer's ancient epic "The Odyssey" into a major cinematic undertaking, sparking widespread discussion about heroism, classical storytelling, and how timeless myths translate to modern audiences. The film, which reportedly cost $250 million, marks an ambitious pivot for the director following his Oscar-winning success with "Oppenheimer."

The project reunites Nolan with actor Matt Damon, who plays Odysseus, the King of Ithaca. The cast also includes Anne Hathaway as Penelope and Tom Holland as Telemachus. The story follows Odysseus's ten-year journey home after the Trojan War, filled with encounters involving monsters, gods, and supernatural obstacles that test both his physical endurance and emotional resilience.

Nolan has explained his motivation for tackling the ancient poem. "The Odyssey underpins almost all of cinema," he stated. "It's certainly there in every movie I've ever done, to a degree I never before realised." The director sees the narrative threads of Homer's epic reflected across filmmaking history, from the hero's journey structure found in everything from "The Wizard of Oz" to "Star Wars" to the trauma-haunted protagonists that populate his own filmography.

The decision to adapt "The Odyssey" emerged from a family discussion. According to Nolan's producing partner and wife, Emma Thomas, one of their children suggested the project. "All our kids are into classical mythology," Thomas explained. "And one of them, Oliver, really loves these stories. And Oliver said: 'What about The Odyssey? Nobody's really done that in a big movie form.'"

The film has generated considerable critical attention, with publications like The Guardian praising Nolan's ambition in bringing the Homeric legend to the screen. Critics have noted that the adaptation explores the psychological toll of war and the difficult process of homecoming, themes that resonate with contemporary audiences grappling with generational trauma and PTSD.

The question of Odysseus's heroism has become central to discussions surrounding the film. National Geographic consulted classicists to address what scholars argue audiences commonly misunderstand about the original epic and its protagonist. Experts have highlighted how ancient Greek conceptions of heroism differ significantly from modern interpretations, with Odysseus portrayed as a flawed character shaped by trauma and guilt rather than a purely noble figure.

The adaptation arrives at a significant moment culturally. Nolan has previously positioned himself as a champion of theatrical cinema over streaming content. By choosing to adapt one of Western literature's foundational texts at an unprecedented scale, the filmmaker appears to be making a statement about cinema's capacity to deliver transformative storytelling experiences.

The film's release marks the culmination of Nolan's most commercially and critically successful period, suggesting audiences and critics will closely scrutinize how this major gamble has paid off.

cards.headline: Gracie Abrams Releases 'Daughter from Hell' Album With Paul Mescal Collaboration
cards.teaser: Pop singer Gracie Abrams released her new album 'Daughter from Hell,' featuring a track cowritten with actor Paul Mescal and songs addressing her relationship with her mother.
cards.body:
Gracie Abrams released her album 'Daughter from Hell,' which includes an apology to her mother and explores themes of rebellion and family relationships. The BBC reviewed the album, describing the rebellion as lacking edge, while Rolling Stone offered a different perspective on the deeply personal tracks.

The album features a collaboration with actor Paul Mescal, who cowrote one of the tracks. Abrams has described the project as a thank you note to her mother, despite its provocative title. Yahoo and Billboard both highlighted the personal nature of the work and its exploration of mother-daughter dynamics.

cards.headline: Metallica's Lars Ulrich Credits U2's Sphere Residency as Inspiration for Band's Vegas Run
cards.teaser: Metallica drummer Lars Ulrich said he was inspired by U2's Sphere residency when planning the band's upcoming Life Burns Faster shows at the Las Vegas venue.
cards.body:
Metallica drummer Lars Ulrich has credited U2's residency at Las Vegas's Sphere venue as a major influence on the band's own approach to performing at the iconic location. Ulrich expressed his admiration for U2's groundbreaking use of the venue's advanced visual technology and immersive concert experience.

Metallica will launch their Life Burns Faster residency at the Sphere this fall, following in U2's footsteps at the cutting-edge venue known for its innovative performances and state-of-the-art production capabilities.

cards.headline: Ariana Grande Brings Out Ty Dolla $ign for Surprise Duet During Brooklyn Show
cards.teaser: Ariana Grande surprised fans during her Brooklyn residency by inviting Ty Dolla $ign onstage to perform their collaboration 'Safety Net.'
cards.body:
Ariana Grande brought out surprise guest Ty Dolla $ign during her Eternal Sunshine Tour stop in Brooklyn on Thursday. The two artists performed their duet "Safety Net" together live, creating an unexpected moment for concertgoers who weren't anticipating the guest appearance.

The collaboration was a standout moment from Grande's Brooklyn residency, adding an unannounced element of excitement to the scheduled show.

cards.headline: Larry David Mocks RFK Jr. in HBO Sketch Show Reuniting 'Curb' Cast
cards.teaser: Larry David used his new HBO sketch comedy series to mock Robert F. Kennedy Jr., saying 'Drop Dead, Bobby' in a show that reunites the 'Curb Your Enthusiasm' cast except for Cheryl Hines.
cards.body:
Larry David weaponizes history to mock Robert F. Kennedy Jr. in his HBO sketch comedy show 'Life, Larry and the Pursuit of Unhappiness: An Almost History of America.' The fourth episode, now streaming on HBO Max, features David taking aim at Kennedy, who is married to David's former 'Curb Your Enthusiasm' costar Cheryl Hines.

The show reunites much of the 'Curb' cast, with the notable exception of Hines. David's willingness to mock Kennedy publicly represents a shift in his relationship with his former colleague's husband. The sketch series uses historical settings as a framework for David's comedy.

cards.headline: Tom Brady Slaps Logan Paul After Panel at Fanatics Fest in New York
cards.teaser: Tom Brady slapped Logan Paul in the face following a heated exchange after their panel ended at Fanatics Fest in New York.
cards.body:
Tom Brady and Logan Paul shared the stage at Fanatics Fest in New York on Friday, but their appearance ended with a physical confrontation. After the panel concluded, the former NFL quarterback and WWE superstar got into a heated exchange that culminated with Brady slapping Paul in the face.

Brady later called Paul a dork and nerd on the social media platform X, continuing their public feud. New York Knicks star players were also present at the event. The confrontation between the future NFL Hall of Famer and the YouTuber-turned-wrestler added an unexpected element to the sports and entertainment convention.

cards.headline: Documentary Examines Impact of Wham!'s 1985 China Concerts
cards.teaser: Andrew Ridgeley says Wham!'s concerts in China changed lives, according to a new documentary about the band's groundbreaking 1985 visit.
cards.body:
A new documentary explores the impact Wham! had on people during their historic visit to China. Andrew Ridgeley, the band's surviving member, discussed how the concerts affected Chinese audiences who had limited exposure to Western pop music at the time.

The 1985 trip marked one of the first times a major Western pop act performed in China. The documentary shows how the visit influenced a generation of Chinese music fans and cultural figures.

hero.headline: US military expands strikes on Iranian infrastructure as tensions escalate
hero.body:
The United States has intensified its aerial campaign against Iran, hitting bridges, ports, and energy facilities as part of an expanded military operation. On Friday, American airstrikes struck bridges in Iran's southern Hormozgan province that serve as key transit points for Bandar Abbas, the nation's main port. The strikes killed at least seven people according to Iranian state television.

Additional US attacks targeted infrastructure at Chabahar port on the Gulf of Oman, where the military claimed the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps used facilities to coordinate attacks on vessels in the Strait of Hormuz. The campaign also struck electrical infrastructure and Iranshahr airport. Following the strikes on power facilities, Iran's energy ministry urged citizens to reduce electricity consumption as the power grid experienced strain, with the southern regions facing extreme heat compounded by damage to power infrastructure.

The strikes represent a significant escalation in scope. Human rights experts have warned that attacks on civilian infrastructure not used for military purposes could constitute war crimes. By Friday morning, Iranian health ministry spokesperson Hossein Kermanpour reported that renewed US strikes had killed at least 38 people and wounded more than 400.

The expanded campaign appears connected to President Donald Trump's stated intention to target Iranian infrastructure and power plants. Reports indicate Trump met with senior department officials this week to discuss an aerial campaign aimed at forcing Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, a critical waterway that handles approximately one-fifth of the world's oil and gas supply before the conflict began.

The fighting has now entered its seventh consecutive day and has undermined an interim deal signed between the countries last month intended to keep the strait open for negotiations toward a permanent truce. Iran has shut the strait while the US reimposed a blockade of Iranian ports and ships as of Wednesday.

In response to Friday's strikes, the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps warned of a "devastating price" for countries hosting US military bases if attacks on infrastructure continued. Iran subsequently targeted multiple US allies across the region, striking Bahrain, Kuwait, Jordan, Oman, and Qatar. In Kuwait, strikes damaged a power and desalination plant that supplies approximately 90 percent of the nation's drinking water.

The fighting has disrupted global shipping significantly. Cargo shipments through the Strait of Hormuz dropped by nearly a quarter at the month's beginning. A tanker traveling near Oman came under attack on Friday, sustaining minor damage though no crew were injured. Iranian state media reported the US also struck an empty oil tanker docked at Kharg Island, Iran's primary oil export terminal.

The escalating violence has driven up fuel prices in the United States, with diesel reaching over five dollars per gallon and regular gasoline approaching four dollars, nearly a dollar and a quarter higher than a year ago.

cards.headline: Iranian strikes injure US troops at Jordan bases
cards.teaser: Several American service members were injured when Iranian forces attacked at least two military installations in Jordan this week.
cards.body:
Iranian attacks struck at least two US military facilities in Jordan this week, injuring several American service members, according to CBS News.

The US and Jordan reported no deaths from the incidents. Iran has continued retaliatory strikes across the region, including attacks on infrastructure in Kuwait. The escalating exchanges between the US and Iran have expanded to include strikes on bridges and renewed tensions over control of the Strait of Hormuz.

cards.headline: Federal judges set guidelines for attorney use of artificial intelligence
cards.teaser: Courts are establishing rules for how lawyers can use AI tools after multiple attorneys have been sanctioned for citing fake cases.
cards.body:
Federal judges have begun setting formal guidelines for attorneys and litigants using artificial intelligence in their courtrooms. The rules come as courts have sanctioned multiple lawyers for submitting AI-generated legal research that included fabricated case citations.

Judges themselves are navigating how to use AI technology in their own chambers. Some have embraced the tools as potential aids to the legal process, while others remain skeptical about incorporating the technology into judicial work. The courts are attempting to balance the benefits of new technology against the need for accuracy and reliability in legal proceedings.

---

Note: The additional source materials provided are about unrelated stories (Moroccan intelligence/Pegasus spyware and parental leave), so the original card text has been returned unchanged.

cards.headline: Trump releases classified documents on election security, claims vulnerabilities exist
cards.teaser: President Trump declassified intelligence documents alleging foreign election interference capabilities, though agencies found no votes were altered in 2020.
cards.body:
President Trump delivered a speech releasing selectively declassified documents about election security, alleging that China interfered in the 2020 election he lost to Joe Biden. He highlighted potential vulnerabilities in American voting systems. China denied the allegations, calling them fabricated.

The intelligence community has maintained that no votes were altered in the 2020 election. Democratic officials criticized the disclosure as an attempt to undermine confidence in upcoming elections. The documents presented largely did not reveal new information or provide evidence that past election results were fraudulent or that actual interference changed previous outcomes.

cards.headline: AIPAC suspends fundraising for House Democrats who voted against Israel aid
cards.teaser: The lobbying group has halted campaign support for over two dozen members who backed cutting billions in military assistance.
cards.body:
The American Israel Public Affairs Committee has stopped fundraising efforts for more than two dozen House Democrats who voted to reduce US military aid to Israel. The lawmakers supported an amendment to the fiscal 2027 State Department funding bill that would have cut billions of dollars in assistance.

More than 100 House Democrats voted in favor of the amendment earlier in the week. AIPAC had previously endorsed and provided financial support to many of the representatives who backed the measure. The suspension represents a significant shift in the organization's relationship with Democratic lawmakers it had supported in previous election cycles.

cards.headline: Paul Pelosi charged with misdemeanor hit-and-run
cards.teaser: The husband of former House Speaker Nancy Pelosi faces charges after allegedly crashing into a parked car and leaving the scene.
cards.body:
Paul Pelosi, husband of former House Speaker Nancy Pelosi, was charged with a misdemeanor hit-and-run on Friday. He allegedly crashed into a parked vehicle in early July and left the scene. The struck car, which was unoccupied, sustained major damage.

Under California law, drivers involved in collisions causing property damage must remain at the scene and provide their license information. A family spokesperson said Paul Pelosi apologized to the vehicle's owner and is assuming responsibility for the damages. Public records show he has had traffic infractions in California dating back to at least 2011.

cards.headline: Milwaukee County executive reenters Wisconsin governor race after lieutenant governor exits
cards.teaser: David Crowley is returning to the Democratic primary following Sara Rodriguez's withdrawal over campaign finance issues.
cards.body:
Milwaukee County Executive David Crowley announced he will rejoin the Democratic primary race for Wisconsin governor. The decision follows the Friday exit of Lieutenant Governor Sara Rodriguez, who ended her campaign over a scandal related to campaign finance errors.

Crowley had previously been a candidate in the race before stepping aside. He indicated on social media that he would make a major campaign announcement. Rodriguez's sudden departure has reshaped the Democratic field in the gubernatorial contest.
